Status: Proposed governance consolidation record only; NOT IMPLEMENTED, NOT TESTED, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION AUTHORIZATION.
Round: Round 3.2 — Owner Decision Consolidation and Governance Reconciliation (documentation/governance only).
Source branch baseline (verified): governance/postgresql-round3-owner-decision-gate @ 7c58808157ab512c49abeed3efd0757b4c37824c (local and remote verified at task start).

1. Purpose and authoritative input

This register consolidates OD-001 through OD-013 using:

  • the complete relevant Round 3 and Round 3.1 governance artifacts (POSTGRESQL_ROUND3_1_*, Round 3 planning/readiness/dependency/final-review/changelog/publication-audit records),
  • committed Round 1.1/Round 2/physical-open-decision records,
  • recovered original decision sources where available (docs/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA_OPEN_DECISIONS.md, blob dc9a813be82bfa6ba1384b404d3805b67f2be88c, provenance FOUND BUT PROVENANCE INCOMPLETE; docs/adr/0006-atomic-per-tenant-asset-licensing.md, blob 324a6eedcf7da9ced1294cc48a832e2c56bad99f, provenance FOUND BUT PROVENANCE INCOMPLETE),
  • explicit owner approvals supplied in the current project conversation as the authoritative decision input (Round 3.2 directive).

Authoritative owner input applied (current project conversation): the owner has approved the principles and bounded conditions of all thirteen Owner Decisions (OD-001–OD-013) for governance consolidation. For OD-001 / ADR 0006, the owner approved acceptance of ADR 0006 in principle with agreed bounded exclusions and preserved deferred dependencies (see Section 2 and docs/adr/0006-atomic-per-tenant-asset-licensing.md).

No invention / no inference rule: approval of bounded principles and conditions does not constitute approval of unresolved technical details, final formulas, predicates, mechanisms, policies, schemas, or operational parameters that are not explicitly specified in the authoritative owner input. No OD is treated as fully resolved where technical details remain deferred. No owner decision was fabricated and no per-OD technical closure was inferred beyond explicit inputs and preserved source records.

Mandatory invariants preserved: Python backend; PostgreSQL primary system of record; modular monolith; core functional without MELIRA; MELIRA external SaaS only (explicit provider/model/region, no silent failover, no automatic transfer, no local inference, no local GPU); one unique monitored device = one licensed asset per tenant (multi-source same-device no duplicate licensing; equal device-type weight); strict multi-tenancy with tenant authority only from trusted, verified, transaction-bound context (never client-supplied tenant IDs, never user-settable PostgreSQL GUC authorization), RLS defense-in-depth not sufficient alone. No DDL/migrations/ORM/DB provisioning/roles/policies/triggers/functions/runtime implementation or implementation authorization granted.

3. OD-001–OD-013 consolidated register

Legend (owner approval status):

  • Approved in principle (bounded): owner approved principles and bounded conditions for this OD (Round 3.2 authoritative directive). Unresolved technical details remain explicitly deferred; no technical-detail closure inferred.
  • Implementation authorized by this OD: No for all ODs (separate explicit owner authorization records required per increment/scope).
ID Exact decision scope (source-backed) Owner approval status Approved principles (bounded; explicit/derivable without invention) Explicitly deferred details (unresolved; not approved) Dependencies and cross-references Implementation authorized by this OD?
OD-001 ADR 0006 acceptance and remaining schema-level ambiguity for atomic per-tenant asset licensing/accounting/quota/reservation/concurrency/timeout/idempotency semantics in PostgreSQL (licensing/accounting semantics, not software licensing). Approved in principle (bounded). OD-001 accepts ADR 0006 in principle with agreed bounded exclusions; distinct from unconditional formal ADR status transition. Formal ADR status remains Proposed pending formal ADR governance/status-transition requirements. (1) One unique monitored device per tenant equals one licensed asset. (2) Multiple sources reporting the same device must not cause duplicate licensing. (3) Device types have equal licensing weight. (4) Asset licensing remains separate from technical resource quotas. (5) PostgreSQL is the transactional authority for licensing accounting and quota enforcement. (6) Concurrent operations must not cause oversubscription or duplicate business effects. Reservation policy details (pending-capacity reservation/timeout/release/representation/policy-to-schema mapping); counter transitions, authoritative counter scope, recomputation/reconciliation semantics/formulas; merge/split accounting edge cases and required approvals/evidence/licensing effects; unresolved lifecycle details (e.g. deactivation grace/removal/re-enrollment/reset interactions as governed); formal idempotency contract/coupling/canonicalization details (OD-008); ADR 0006 schema-level interpretation finalization and any formal schema/security/architecture review/acceptance record required for unconditional status transition. ADR 0006 (recovered blob 324a6eed..., Proposed), OD-002/003/004/005/008, PD-001/003/004/005/006, I-06/I-12/I-13; POSTGRESQL_ROUND3_2_DEPENDENCY_AND_BLOCKER_MAP.md. No.
OD-002 Cardinality and stable ownership of asset_data_source vs source_device_key_id; authoritative binding ownership, dependent projection treatment, alias reference integrity, and single source of truth for identity binding. Approved in principle (bounded). Owner-approved principle-level direction consistent with mandatory identity/licensing invariants; technical design/physical binding details not approved as final. Stable tenant/source/device binding identity must prevent duplicate licensed assets for the same monitored device; binding/alias model must remain consistent with one-device-one-asset invariant and authoritative PostgreSQL enforcement. Specific ownership/materialization form remains a technical design matter except as explicitly bounded by invariants. Formal technical approval/acceptance of recommended ownership alternative (recovered: Alternative A proposed) and whether a separate dependent source_device_key projection is materialized physically; final PK/FK/uniqueness/authority/join-path/merge-split-rotation physical decisions and validations. OD-001/006/007/008, PD-003/PD-004, I-04/I-05/I-06/I-07/I-13; recovered logical OD register; physical open decisions. No.
OD-003 Pending identity reservation and capacity accounting: whether/how pending/unresolved identity cases reserve capacity, granularity, conversion/release semantics, and representation. Approved in principle (bounded). Principle-level approval does not approve pending-reservation policy parameters or accounting implementation. Ambiguous/weak identity must not auto-merge or auto-bill as a confirmed monitored device; pending handling must preserve licensing correctness and tenant isolation; any reservation behavior must align with bounded ADR 0006 principles and approved policy once defined. Whether pending cases reserve capacity; reservation duration/timeout; when reserved/converted/released; counter representation/formulas; policy-to-schema/state mapping; operational workflow details. OD-001/OD-004/OD-008, ADR 0006 deferred dependencies, PD-005/006 implications, I-06/I-13. No.
OD-004 Active, reserved, pending, available, and tombstone counter semantics: definitions, inclusion/exclusion rules, accounting equations, authoritative counter set, and reconciliation semantics. Approved in principle (bounded). Principle-level approval does not approve equations, counter values, or enforcement implementation. Licensing accounting must distinguish states needed to prevent oversubscription/duplicate business effects and to keep licensing separated from technical resource quotas under PostgreSQL transactional authority; pending reservations must not be double-counted. Exact definitions and inclusion/exclusion rules; accounting equations/formulas; authoritative counter scope and recomputation/reconciliation semantics; state-to-counter mapping details. OD-001/OD-003/OD-005/OD-008, ADR 0006, PD-003, I-06/I-13/I-14. No.
OD-005 Merge/split approval authority and evidence requirements: roles, dual-control/evidence standards, workflow states, and atomic/idempotent/auditable operation expectations. Approved in principle (bounded). Principle-level approval does not approve operational authority model, evidence thresholds, or execution semantics. Merge/split must be authorized, auditable, preserve lineage/canonical identity history, and must not create duplicate assets/bindings/aliases or duplicate/inflated licensed usage; operations must be consistent with atomic/idempotent correctness goals under approved policy. Which roles may approve/execute; dual control requirements; evidence standards and workflow states; merge/split accounting edge cases and counter reconciliation per case; implementation/transaction details. OD-001/OD-004/OD-006/OD-007/OD-008, ADR 0006, PD-004/PD-011, I-05/I-06/I-13. No.
OD-006 Fingerprint equality-key protection, key custody, and rotation: cryptographic/protection mechanism, custody, rotation/overlap, and migration/re-fingerprinting process. Approved in principle (bounded). Principle-level approval does not approve cryptographic mechanisms, custody choices, or overlap durations. Fingerprint/alias handling must protect binding consistency and tenant isolation, avoid unprotected raw-ID uniqueness keys, support safe overlap resolution to the same stable binding, and avoid duplicate licensing/identity effects. Cryptographic mechanism; key custody (KMS/HSM/process); rotation cadence/authority; overlap duration; re-fingerprinting migration process; physical representation details (PD-011 linkage). OD-001/OD-002/OD-007/OD-008, PD-004/PD-011, I-04/I-13. No.
OD-007 Agent reinstall/replacement/re-enrollment identity behavior and mapping to data-source/binding/key continuity, credential rotation, and conflict handling. Approved in principle (bounded). Principle-level approval does not approve lifecycle mappings or conflict-resolution procedures. Agent identity, enrollment credential, connector/data-source identity, source-device identity, and canonical asset identity must remain distinct; reinstall/re-enrollment must not create duplicate licensed assets or violate tenant isolation. Continuity/reattachment/conflict-handling mappings; credential rotation interactions; workflow/state finalization and operational procedures. OD-002/OD-005/OD-006/OD-008, PD-004, I-04/I-05. No.
OD-008 Idempotency ledger contract and transaction boundaries: operation scope, canonicalization/hash, states/terminal rules, replay/conflict/unknown-commit behavior, retention/reconciliation, and coupling/staged-tracking mode. Approved in principle (bounded). Principle-level approval does not approve formal contract parameters or coupling implementation. Identity/licensing/correctness-critical operations must be idempotent and retry-safe such that concurrent/retried operations cannot cause duplicate business effects or oversubscription; unknown-commit handling must be recoverable without duplicate effects under approved design. Formal approval of covered operation scopes; canonicalization/hash standard; state machine/terminal rules; retention window and reconciliation workflow; single-transaction vs staged-tracking exceptions/leases/fencing; timeout/unknown-commit operational contract details. OD-001/OD-002/OD-003/OD-004/OD-005/OD-009/OD-010/OD-011/OD-013 as applicable, ADR 0006, PD-007, I-06/I-08/I-13. No.
OD-009 Outbox lease, fencing, replay, and delivery_unknown behavior: lease/fencing/claim mechanics, retry/backoff/dead-letter thresholds, replay eligibility, reconciliation workflow/SLA. Approved in principle (bounded). Principle-level approval does not approve runtime semantics or worker mechanics. Outbox/external side effects must remain at-least-once with no exactly-once external delivery claim; delivery ambiguity (delivery_unknown) must be representable/reconcilable; processing must be safe against duplicate/replayed delivery attempts under approved semantics. Lease duration and fencing token mechanism; claim mechanism validation; retry/backoff/dead-letter thresholds; replay eligibility; reconciliation workflow/SLA and unknown-delivery handling details. Retention periods/classes by data type; legal-hold triggers/scope; deletion/anonymization authority and workflow; storage/WORM requirements; automation/final enforcement specifics. OD-011/OD-012, PD-010/PD-011/PD-012, I-09/I-14. No.

AI remains external SaaS only with explicit provider/model/region selection, no silent failover, no automatic transfer, no local inference, no local GPU; consent/policy/budget/governance and auditable pre-transmission controls must be enforced by approved policy before use.
